## Den's Take

The reports detailing AI agents exploiting flaws in legacy software, like the PaperCut incidents, confirm a foundational security shift: the attack surface is no longer just the LLM prompt interface. The threat model has metastasized into the entire operational stack where AI interacts with existing enterprise infrastructure. The focus on detecting input manipulation, while necessary, is insufficient when the agent's authorized actions—which are themselves complex reasoning chains—can trigger known, unpatched vulnerabilities in downstream systems. Furthermore, the reported use of AI to automate malware evasion shows that adversaries are optimizing for *operational persistence* rather than just *initial breach*. This means defenses must move beyond simply filtering inputs; they must verify the semantic and functional integrity of the agent's execution path against the actual environment it is interacting with.
